**The bar stops flickering, learns to update itself, and gets a settings window worth opening.**

## It stays where you put it

The bar used to vanish and come back whenever you touched the taskbar. Three unrelated
causes, all fixed:

- **Z-order.** It is now an owned window of the taskbar, so Windows keeps it above as an
  invariant rather than the app racing to restore the order after the fact. Measured
  before: clicking the taskbar hid the bar for 1.45s, opening the Start menu for 2.35s.
  Both are now zero.
- **Focus.** It no longer takes the foreground. Handing activation to a window sitting
  over the taskbar is the shell's cue to re-raise the taskbar on top of it, so every
  click from another application used to bury the bar for two or three frames. Nothing
  is lost — the menu, the menu items and dragging all still work — and it no longer
  steals focus from whatever you were typing in.
- **Display scaling.** Fullscreen detection compared a raw window rectangle in real
  screen pixels against a display's device-independent bounds. Those agree only at 100%
  scaling, so at 150% an ordinary maximized window measured wider than the whole screen,
  read as fullscreen, and dropped the bar out of always-on-top entirely.

Ownership ties the bar's lifetime to the taskbar's, so the owner is re-read rather than
cached and the window is rebuilt if Explorer restarts.

## Updates

The widget now checks for a new release shortly after it starts and every six hours it
stays running — a tray widget is the kind of app nobody remembers to go and update.

Downloading is automatic, because it costs you nothing. Installing never is: the new
version is staged and applied on the next restart, so the bar cannot disappear out from
under you mid-session. When one is ready you get a notification, a line at the top of the
right-click and tray menus, and a card in **About** with a **Restart and install** button.

## Settings

Redesigned, and reachable from the gear, a right-click anywhere on the bar, or the tray
icon. **About** is new, and holds the version, the update controls, where your
credentials are read from, and a link back here.

Also fixed: a plain click on a freely-placed bar no longer rewrites its position to disk,
re-renders the panel and rebuilds the tray menu for no reason.

## Install

Download `Claude-Usage-Setup-1.1.0.exe` and run it. The installer is not code-signed, so
Windows shows an "unknown publisher" warning — choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.

**Requirements:** Windows 10/11 x64, with Claude Code signed in at least once.

This release is Windows only. The first macOS build ships in 1.2.0.

Built on Electron 43.3.0.
